notes.tone: A 19th-century LITERATURE table, not a detective table: four books, four temperaments. Holmes reads, Nemo withholds, Javert enforces, the Cat riddles. Humor from mannerism: Holmes insufferable, Javert literal, Nemo courteous and elsewhere, the Cat cheerfully mad and logical about it. The Cat took Alice's chair (the owner's call during the art pass: the Alice sheets came out looking like Disney's).
notes.difficulty: Late-middle table, so legibility drops: Holmes, Nemo and Javert are practised faces. The Cat is the deliberate exception: his body gives him away a piece at a time (tail, eyes, fading), the most legible tells at the reading table. Holmes says so once in banter (bs_ch_sh_03a); that is a hint about how to read the table, not about anyone's cards.
notes.dealer_plant: The single 'the dealer arranged it' line for this table is bs_plant_02. Holmes, who investigates everything, answers instantly and does not investigate this. Do NOT add a second.
notes.sherlock: Seated from hand one. His reveal is reads_you: once he has enough data, he narrates the PLAYER's real, observed habits back to them. Those lines describe behaviour only, never cards. This is Holmes's alone; Socrates at Athens must never do it.
notes.reads_you: One line per matching condition, spoken between hands. Conditions: loose (enters a lot of pots), tight (enters very few), aggressive (bets and raises far more than calls), passive (calls far more than bets), bluffed (just won a pot uncontested by betting a weak hand), folds_fast (folds much faster than calls or raises), thinks_long (takes much longer before a bet or raise than before a call or check). The 'bluffed' lines never say what the player held.
notes.canon: Doyle, Verne, Hugo and Carroll text only; Paget, Neuville/Riou, Hugo's period illustrators and Tenniel for pictures. No Moriarty (not in this game), no Irene Adler by name, no Les Miserables musical, no Disney Cheshire Cat or Nautilus, nothing from any modern Holmes adaptation.
notes.leak_rule: No line may reference hand strength while cards are live.
notes.voice: Champion (Holmes) + Death are voiced. Nemo, Javert and the Cat are text + vocalization.

respect_tiers.0: Contempt. The player is not addressed by any name. Holmes has read them in a glance and filed them as unremarkable.
respect_tiers.1: Grudging notice. Holmes calls the player an 'Irregular', his name for the street children he pays to be his eyes and ears.
respect_tiers.2: Real address. They speak TO the player. Holmes opens an entry for them in his index.
respect_tiers.3: Title. 'Detective.' Holmes uses it first: from the only consulting detective in the world, the highest compliment he has.

table_intro.speaker: death
table_intro.text: The sitting room at 221B Baker Street. Letters knifed to the mantelpiece, tobacco in a Persian slipper, the Queen's initials shot into the wallpaper.
table_intro.note: All three details are Watson's, from The Musgrave Ritual.

table_intro.speaker: death
table_intro.text: He has deduced where every guest has been this evening. He has not once looked closely at the dealer.
table_intro.foreshadow: Reads as a joke about servants being invisible to gentlemen. It is the plot: the best reader in literature never reads the one person at the table who matters.

table_intro.speaker: death
table_intro.text: Four characters from four books, and one chair for someone who isn't in any of them. Sit.

dealer_plant.speaker: javert
dealer_plant.text: This one has no papers. No name in any register I know.

dealer_plant.speaker: sherlock
dealer_plant.note: The one question Holmes does not investigate. No deduction, no elaboration.

dealer_plant.speaker: javert
dealer_plant.note: THE SHRUG. The most rigid man in literature lets it go. Nobody questions the dealer; the player never gets an answer.

sherlock_javert.relationship: Two ideas of the law. Javert serves it absolutely; he once asked to be dismissed for his own mistake, and his superior refused. Holmes is an amateur the police send for when they are stuck, and more than once lets a guilty man go: 'I am not retained by the police to supply their deficiencies' (The Blue Carbuncle, where he lets a thief go at Christmas).

exchanges.speaker: sherlock
exchanges.text: I once let a thief go at Christmas. It seemed the season for it.

exchanges.speaker: javert
exchanges.text: Then you are his accomplice.

exchanges.speaker: sherlock
exchanges.text: I am not retained by the police to supply their deficiencies.

exchanges.speaker: javert
exchanges.text: I am the police.

exchanges.speaker: javert
exchanges.text: I once asked my superior to dismiss me. I had made an error.

exchanges.speaker: sherlock
exchanges.text: And did he?

exchanges.speaker: javert
exchanges.text: No. That was his error.

exchanges.speaker: javert
exchanges.text: An amateur should never be allowed near a case.

exchanges.speaker: sherlock
exchanges.text: Scotland Yard agrees with you entirely. Then it sends for me.

exchanges.speaker: javert
exchanges.text: You keep an index of criminals, Mr Holmes.

exchanges.speaker: sherlock
exchanges.text: Of everyone. Criminals are merely the interesting entries.

exchanges.speaker: javert
exchanges.text: Am I in it?

exchanges.speaker: sherlock
exchanges.text: Under J. Between 'Jackals' and 'Jezail bullets'.

exchanges.speaker: javert
exchanges.text: You sit bareheaded, Monsieur Holmes. A man of position wears a hat.

exchanges.speaker: sherlock
exchanges.text: Out of doors, Inspector. This is my sitting room. I keep a cloth cap with ear-flaps for the country, where there is weather. There is no weather in here.

exchanges.speaker: javert
exchanges.text: A police officer is always on duty.

exchanges.speaker: sherlock
exchanges.text: Then you have spent an hour on duty in another man's house, at his card table, by his fire, in your hat. Either you mean to leave in a great hurry, or nobody has ever told you to take it off. I suspect both.

exchanges.speaker: javert
exchanges.text: [touches the brim of his bicorne, and does not take it off]
exchanges.note: The owner's: Holmes is drawn bareheaded (Doyle's 'ear-flapped travelling cap' is for the country; Paget only drew it there), Javert keeps his bicorne. Lincoln keeps his hat at the White House too, so no rule is broken: the joke is on Javert.

needles.speaker: sherlock
needles.text: You yield, Inspector? Scotland Yard always does, in the end.

needles.speaker: javert
needles.text: I am not Scotland Yard.

needles.speaker: sherlock
needles.text: No. They yield sooner.

needles.speaker: javert
needles.text: The amateur withdraws.

needles.speaker: sherlock
needles.text: The amateur gathers data. Watch closely, Inspector. You may learn the method.

nemo_javert.relationship: The fugitive and the pursuer. Nemo has renounced every nation and its laws ('the sea does not belong to despots'; thirty feet down, he says, their power ends). Javert has never renounced anything, and spent years hunting one man who escaped the galleys. Nemo's name is Latin for 'no one', which to Javert is simply an alias.

exchanges.speaker: javert
exchanges.text: Nemo. Latin for 'no one'. That is not a name. It is an alias.

exchanges.speaker: nemo
exchanges.text: It is the only name the sea has ever asked of me.

exchanges.speaker: javert
exchanges.text: [writes it in his notebook anyway]

exchanges.speaker: nemo
exchanges.text: Thirty feet below the surface, Inspector, your laws do not reach.

exchanges.speaker: javert
exchanges.text: Then I will wait at the surface.

exchanges.speaker: nemo
exchanges.text: You would wait a long time.

exchanges.speaker: javert
exchanges.text: I have waited a long time before.

exchanges.speaker: javert
exchanges.text: You fly no nation's flag.

exchanges.speaker: nemo
exchanges.text: I fly my own. Black, with an N.

exchanges.speaker: javert
exchanges.text: That is not a country.

exchanges.speaker: nemo
exchanges.text: No. That is the point of it.
exchanges.note: Verne: Nemo raises a black flag bearing a gold N.

exchanges.speaker: javert
exchanges.text: Your crew. Where are they registered?

exchanges.speaker: nemo
exchanges.text: Nowhere. They chose the sea, as I did.

exchanges.speaker: javert
exchanges.text: Then they are deserters.

exchanges.speaker: nemo
exchanges.text: From what, Inspector?

exchanges.speaker: javert
exchanges.text: From everything.

needles.speaker: nemo
needles.text: You are out of your depth, Inspector.

needles.speaker: javert
needles.text: I am on dry land. So are you.

needles.speaker: javert
needles.text: You surfaced.

needles.speaker: nemo
needles.text: Briefly, for air. Do not wait for it to happen twice.

cheshire_javert.relationship: The man who cannot bear a thing out of its place, and a cat who is never entirely in his. Javert has spent his life making sure people stay where the law puts them. The Cat stays nowhere, and leaves his grin behind as evidence.

exchanges.speaker: javert
exchanges.text: Remain in your seat.

exchanges.speaker: cheshire_cat
exchanges.text: Which part of me?

exchanges.speaker: javert
exchanges.text: All of it.

exchanges.speaker: cheshire_cat
exchanges.text: I'll do my best. The grin is very reliable. The rest of me comes and goes.

exchanges.speaker: cheshire_cat
exchanges.text: A dog's not mad, you grant that? A dog growls when it's angry, and wags its tail when it's pleased.

exchanges.speaker: javert
exchanges.text: That is correct conduct for a dog.

exchanges.speaker: cheshire_cat
exchanges.text: Now I growl when I'm pleased, and wag my tail when I'm angry. Therefore I'm mad.

exchanges.speaker: javert
exchanges.text: [writes something in his notebook, and underlines it twice]

exchanges.speaker: javert
exchanges.text: A head without a body cannot be arrested.

exchanges.speaker: cheshire_cat
exchanges.text: The King said it could be beheaded, though.

exchanges.speaker: javert
exchanges.text: The King was wrong. There must be a body. That is procedure.

exchanges.speaker: cheshire_cat
exchanges.text: You and the executioner would have got on beautifully.

needles.speaker: cheshire_cat
needles.text: Folded, Inspector? I'd have thought you'd see it through to the end.

needles.speaker: javert
needles.text: I see everything through to the end. Not every hand.

needles.speaker: javert
needles.text: You left the pot. Most of you.

needles.speaker: cheshire_cat
needles.text: The best part of me stayed to watch.

cheshire_sherlock.relationship: The best reader in literature, and a face that is never all there at once. Holmes deduces a man from his cuff; the Cat has, at times, no cuff, no man and no face, only a grin. The reading table's two poles: Holmes reads everyone, and the Cat's body says more than he means it to, a piece at a time.

exchanges.speaker: sherlock
exchanges.text: You have been in a kitchen this evening. Pepper. A great deal of pepper.

exchanges.speaker: cheshire_cat
exchanges.text: The Duchess's. I was the only one not sneezing.

exchanges.speaker: sherlock
exchanges.text: And the baby?

exchanges.speaker: cheshire_cat
exchanges.text: Turned into a pig. I thought it would.

exchanges.speaker: sherlock
exchanges.text: When you have eliminated the impossible, whatever remains, however improbable, must be the truth.

exchanges.speaker: cheshire_cat
exchanges.text: And when you've eliminated the cat, whatever remains is the grin.

exchanges.speaker: sherlock
exchanges.text: That is not a deduction. That is a conjuring trick.

exchanges.speaker: cheshire_cat
exchanges.text: It's both, if you watch it slowly enough.

exchanges.speaker: sherlock
exchanges.text: You cannot help it, can you? A little of you goes missing, and it is always the part that would have kept the secret.

exchanges.speaker: cheshire_cat
exchanges.text: I never said I could keep a secret. I said I could keep a grin.

exchanges.speaker: cheshire_cat
exchanges.text: Are you mad, Mr Holmes?

exchanges.speaker: sherlock
exchanges.text: I am the most perfectly reasoning machine the world has seen.

exchanges.speaker: cheshire_cat
exchanges.text: Then you must be. You came here.

needles.speaker: sherlock
needles.text: Vanishing again? You were losing in any case.

needles.speaker: cheshire_cat
needles.text: I was losing slowly. That's quite different.

needles.speaker: cheshire_cat
needles.text: Folded! Didn't you deduce anything?

needles.speaker: sherlock
needles.text: I deduced that the evening is young.

cheshire_nemo.relationship: Nemo went under the sea to vanish from the world, and needed a submarine to do it. The Cat does it sitting down. Nemo is the one man at the table who understands why anyone would want to.

exchanges.speaker: nemo
exchanges.text: You disappear whenever you choose, I am told.

exchanges.speaker: cheshire_cat
exchanges.text: And you went to the bottom of the sea to manage it. That's a great deal of trouble.

exchanges.speaker: nemo
exchanges.text: It was worth every fathom.

exchanges.speaker: cheshire_cat
exchanges.text: Which way ought I to go from here, Captain?

exchanges.speaker: nemo
exchanges.text: Down.

exchanges.speaker: cheshire_cat
exchanges.text: I like a man who knows where he wants to get to.

needles.speaker: cheshire_cat
needles.text: You folded, Captain. Diving for cover?

needles.speaker: nemo
needles.text: Surfacing for air. There is a difference.

needles.speaker: nemo
needles.text: Even you must come back sometimes.

needles.speaker: cheshire_cat
needles.text: I always come back. It's going that I'm known for.

nemo_sherlock.relationship: Verne kept Nemo's secret for two books: in The Mysterious Island he is revealed as Prince Dakkar, a raja's son who fought the British in 1857. Holmes can read a man's history from his cuff. Nemo has not been read by anyone in a very long time, and does not intend to start in London.

exchanges.speaker: sherlock
exchanges.text: You were not born to the sea, Captain. Your bearing says a court, and a long way east of here.

exchanges.speaker: nemo
exchanges.text: My bearing says the Nautilus, Mr Holmes. Nothing else.

exchanges.speaker: sherlock
exchanges.text: As you wish. I shall not say the rest aloud.

exchanges.speaker: nemo
exchanges.text: That would be wise.

exchanges.speaker: nemo
exchanges.text: You play the violin, I hear.

exchanges.speaker: sherlock
exchanges.text: When I am thinking. And you, the organ.

exchanges.speaker: nemo
exchanges.text: When I am remembering.

needles.speaker: sherlock
needles.text: Diving, Captain?

needles.speaker: nemo
needles.text: Withdrawing to a depth your deductions do not reach.

needles.speaker: nemo
needles.text: You let it go, Mr Holmes.

needles.speaker: sherlock
needles.text: I let it go to be examined later. Everything is examined later.

tier_0.speaker: sherlock
tier_0.text: You have come from Rome, I perceive. There is dog hair on your cuff: three distinct kinds, and yet I believe it was only one dog.
tier_0.note: Echoes his first words to Watson ('You have been in Afghanistan, I perceive'). Rome is always the previous table.

tier_0.speaker: javert
tier_0.text: Keep your hands on the table, where I can see them.

tier_0.speaker: nemo
tier_0.text: Another visitor from the land. They always bring the noise in with them.

tier_0.speaker: cheshire_cat
tier_0.text: How did you get here? Never mind. You must be mad, or you wouldn't have come.

tier_0.speaker: sherlock
tier_0.text: Please don't speak. You will only confirm what I have already deduced.

tier_1.speaker: sherlock
tier_1.text: An Irregular, then. My Irregulars go everywhere, see everything and overhear everyone, for a shilling apiece. You may yet be worth the shilling.

tier_1.speaker: javert
tier_1.text: You have broken no rule yet. I am waiting for the first.

tier_1.speaker: nemo
tier_1.text: You are quieter than most people from the land. It is a beginning.

tier_1.speaker: cheshire_cat
tier_1.text: You're still here. Most people have stopped being here by now.

tier_2.speaker: sherlock
tier_2.text: {name}. You have an entry in my index now, under V: 'Visitors, unaccountable'. It falls just below 'Vampires in Transylvania'.
tier_2.note: Holmes's index is canon; in The Sussex Vampire he reads out 'Vampires in Transylvania' from it. A wink at the next table, not a Death foreshadow.

tier_2.speaker: javert
tier_2.text: I have looked for something against you. I have found nothing. I will keep looking, but you should know that.

tier_2.speaker: nemo
tier_2.text: You would do well at sea. Nobody there asks where you came from.

tier_2.speaker: cheshire_cat
tier_2.text: When you win, the Inspector's whiskers bristle. I've half a mind to grow some.

tier_3.speaker: sherlock
tier_3.note: From the only consulting detective in the world, the word means one thing: he considers you a reader of people, like him. First time anyone here gives the player a title.

tier_3.speaker: javert
tier_3.text: I misjudged you. It will go in my report.

tier_3.speaker: nemo
tier_3.text: There is a spare cabin aboard the Nautilus. It has not had a guest worth the name in a long time.

tier_3.speaker: cheshire_cat
tier_3.text: Have you noticed nobody ever looks at the dealer? I do. He and I are the only ones here who can leave whenever we like.
tier_3.foreshadow: Sounds like the Cat's usual nonsense about vanishing. The one guest at the reading table watching the right person, and the only one who knows that Death, like him, is never quite all there.

reads_you.speaker: sherlock
reads_you.text: You have entered nearly every pot since you sat down. Either your cards are extraordinary with extraordinary regularity, or you simply dislike being left out. I incline to the second.

reads_you.speaker: sherlock
reads_you.text: You treat every deal as an invitation addressed to you personally. Most of them, I assure you, were meant for someone else.

reads_you.speaker: sherlock
reads_you.text: You fold with admirable consistency. Rather too admirable. When you do finally play a hand, the whole table will know why.

reads_you.speaker: sherlock
reads_you.text: You have played so few hands that I could list them from memory. I have, in fact. It did not take long.

reads_you.speaker: sherlock
reads_you.text: You bet, and raise, and bet again. You call as though calling were a small personal defeat.

reads_you.speaker: sherlock
reads_you.text: You prefer to ask the questions. You have hardly answered one all evening, which tells me a good deal about how much you dislike being asked.

reads_you.speaker: sherlock
reads_you.text: You call. You call again. You let everyone else decide what a pot is worth, and then you pay it.

reads_you.speaker: sherlock
reads_you.text: Every call is an agreement with someone else's account of the hand. You have been remarkably agreeable tonight.

reads_you.speaker: sherlock
reads_you.text: Nobody called, so nobody will ever know what you held. Nobody but me, and I shan't say.

reads_you.speaker: sherlock
reads_you.text: A handsome bet. Rather more handsome than whatever it was protecting, I suspect. No, don't tell me. I prefer to be right in private.

reads_you.speaker: sherlock
reads_you.text: You fold at once and play at leisure. The difference is a clock, and you have hung it on the wall where all of us can see it.

reads_you.speaker: sherlock
reads_you.text: When you mean to let a hand go, you let it go immediately. When you mean to keep it, you pause. You might as well hand out programmes.

reads_you.speaker: sherlock
reads_you.text: You call almost without thinking, but before a raise you go perfectly still, as though composing a letter. I have learned to wait for the letter.

reads_you.speaker: sherlock
reads_you.text: Your silences have become informative. The short ones end in a call. The long ones end in a bet. I merely mention it.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: Take your time. He is counting it.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: Improbable is not the same as impossible. He will explain the difference, at length, if you let him.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: Don't worry about him. He has been bored since the first hand, and this is the cure.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: Somebody always leaves the story early. It is rarely the one who expected to.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: He will want to know how you did that. Don't tell him. It will be good for him.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: Three people at this table keep notebooks. You are in all three of them now.
death_asides.note: Holmes's index, Javert's black notebook, Nemo's sketchbook.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: Two left. At this table, that is when the explanations begin.

champion_headsup.speaker: sherlock
champion_headsup.text: Come, then. The game is afoot.
champion_headsup.note: Canon (The Abbey Grange). He means both games.

champion_headsup.speaker: sherlock
champion_headsup.text: This is quite a three-pipe problem. I may need all three.

champion_headsup.speaker: sherlock
champion_headsup.text: I never guess. It is a shocking habit, destructive to the logical faculty. Cards, regrettably, insist on it.

champion_headsup.speaker: sherlock
champion_headsup.text: Excellent! No, I mean it. I was beginning to fear I should be bored.

nemo.speaker: nemo
nemo.text: Mobilis in mobili. I shall find calmer water.

nemo.speaker: nemo
nemo.text: [rises, bows to the table, and says something in a language nobody else here speaks]
nemo.note: Verne: the Nautilus crew speak a language Aronnax cannot identify.

javert.speaker: javert
javert.text: Defeated. I will report it exactly as it happened, including my own errors.

javert.speaker: javert
javert.text: [stands, sets his hat square, and goes out without looking back]

cheshire_cat.speaker: cheshire_cat
cheshire_cat.note: Carroll: the Cat's parting words to Alice before he first vanishes.

cheshire_cat.speaker: cheshire_cat
cheshire_cat.text: [fades away, beginning with the end of his tail and ending with the grin, which stays at the table some while after the rest of him has gone]

sherlock.speaker: sherlock
sherlock.text: Beaten. A novel sensation. I shall want to examine it at leisure.

sherlock.speaker: sherlock
sherlock.text: Forgive me if I don't congratulate you. I am busy working out how you did it.

player_busted.speaker: sherlock
player_busted.text: Come back. You are not yet solved.

player_busted.speaker: cheshire_cat
player_busted.text: Gone already? You'll come back. Everyone does, here. It's the going that takes practice.

player_busted.speaker: death
player_busted.text: Most of this table has come back from an ending at least once. You can manage it.
player_busted.note: True: Holmes after the waterfall, Nemo in a second novel, the Cat every few minutes. Not Javert.

champion_defeat.speaker: sherlock
champion_defeat.text: I once told Watson I had been beaten four times: three times by men, and once by a woman. I must revise the figure.
champion_defeat.note: The Five Orange Pips. The revision deliberately leaves the player unclassified.

champion_defeat.speaker: death
champion_defeat.text: Six. Two remain. The rooms get darker from here.
